Choose a concentric pad or ground-stitched CPW model, then use the matching
AEDT tutorial. Its QMD defines the exact runtime, geometry, and numerical controls.

⏳ Native execution of these revised examples is pending. Use their source and
model descriptions to prepare a calculation; keep earlier saved results with their original models.

## System and representation

- **Concentric system:** annular Signal pads on both die faces connect through
  the central hollow TSV. Four surrounding TSVs connect the two separate Ground
  planes. The Signal opening and bore are not Ground.
- **Ground-stitched CPW:** a through Signal reaches the two exterior cuts; two
  rows of TSVs stitch top and back Ground. It is a full 3D system, not a uniform
  Q2D section or a claim of optimal TSV spacing.
- **Model:** face metal/landings use Thin Film. Hollow TiN walls and cut Silicon
  remain finite Solid. The physical source thickness and material identity stay
  recorded; the backend handles declared source-to-effective Z mapping.

The canonical factories in `orcapen_sc_pdk.cells.simulation.scgsim.tsv` own shapes,
holes, source occurrences and contact intent. Concrete dimensions,
Net membership and enclosure controls live in each notebook.

## Use the workflow actions

- `run` prepares a new layout and handoff, invokes the native solve, and reads returned results.
- `prepare_handoff` stops at portable inputs.
- `analyze_handoff` reads the explicitly selected returned directory without rebuilding geometry.
- `build_model` and `inspect_model` are separate model-only actions.

Inspect body/sheet assignments, hollow walls, substrate holes, Nets, and
port references in the actual native model. Keep the model-only view separate
from solved quantities. For interpreting the result, read
[Capacitance](requirements/electrostatic-capacitance.qmd),
[Resonance & Eigenmodes](requirements/eigenmode.qmd), or
[S-parameters & Ports](requirements/driven-terminal.qmd).
